## LU pivot tolerance: refuse a pivot within $8N\epsilon$ of its row (`ludcmp`) {#sec-ch07-vic-pivot}

<!-- PROVENANCE

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Refuses to factor a VIC block when a pivot is, relative to the original size of its row, no
bigger than the rounding error of the elimination, or when anything in the factorisation is not finite.
**Switch.** None.
**Order.** Not a discretisation.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch07-vic-pivot.
:::

`ludcmp` is the Crout factorisation with scaled partial pivoting. It returns the sign of the row permutation, or
0 for a refusal. The refusal turns into a failed column (@sec-ch07-vic-sweep), which turns into a rejected step
(@sec-ch07-vic-reject).

### Derivation

Let $s_j$ be the largest magnitude in the original row that ends up in position $j$, and $p_j$ the pivot found
there. The factorisation is refused when

$$
\frac{|p_j|}{s_j} \le \tau_N , \quad \tau_N = 8N\epsilon_T ,
$$ {#eq-ch07-vic-pivot}

with $\epsilon_T$ the machine epsilon of the scalar type (`epsilon_T` in the note), the last pivot included. A dot product of length about
$2N$ accumulates a relative rounding error of about $N\epsilon_T$. The factor 8 is a guard band around that
scale, as the derivation note argues with `epsilon_T`
([`290-lu-pivot-tolerance.md:18-26`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/docs/derivations/290-lu-pivot-tolerance.md#L18-L26)).
The values are $2.861\times10^{-6}$ and $4.768\times10^{-6}$ in float, and $5.329\times10^{-15}$ and
$8.882\times10^{-15}$ in double, for $N=3$ and 5 [check `src/snapy_report/ch07/vic_pivot_check.py`, output
`vic_pivot_check.out`, `[C1]`]. A ratio $0.99\,\tau_3$ is refused and $1.01\,\tau_3$ accepted, in both types
(`[C2]`).

Because $p_j$ and $s_j$ scale together, the decision does not depend on the units of a row. With power-of-two
row factors, which are exact in floating point, no decision of 400 random matrices changes. With decimal factors
one borderline case flips by rounding (`[C3]`). A pivot ratio of $1.25\times10^{-6}$ passes in double and is
refused in float32 (`[C4]`).

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch07-vic-pivot for the threshold.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch07-vic-pivot
#| fig-cap: "ludcmp on the $3\\times3$ test matrix of the check as its last pivot ratio $|p_j|/s_j$ is swept: dots are accepted, crosses (vermillion) refused. The dashed lines are $\\tau_3=24\\epsilon_T$ for float64 (blue) and float32 (orange); the refusals end exactly there."
#| fig-alt: "Two horizontal rows of markers, float64 and float32, against a log axis of pivot ratio; crosses to the left of each dashed threshold line and dots to its right."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch07.fig_vic_pivot import make_fig
make_fig()
```

`ludcmp` refuses a nonfinite input first, with `isfinite` ([`ludcmp.h:36-38`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/math/ludcmp.h#L36-L38)). It then refuses a zero
row or a nonfinite row reciprocal `vv` ([`ludcmp.h:41-49`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/math/ludcmp.h#L41-L49)). During the elimination it refuses a nonfinite partial
sum, and it carries the original row scale `scale` through the row swaps ([`ludcmp.h:70-81`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/math/ludcmp.h#L70-L81)). The test
itself is one line, through `tolerance` ([`ludcmp.h:83`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/math/ludcmp.h#L83)). A last scan with `isfinite` refuses a
nonfinite factor ([`ludcmp.h:90-93`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/math/ludcmp.h#L90-L93)).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The guard is a pivot safety check, not a condition-number estimate. An accepted block can still be badly
conditioned, and acceptance does not mean an accurate step.
:::

1. **Float32.** The guard is about $5\times10^8$ times stricter in `float32`. The derivation note records an independent
   probe of random 3 x 3 matrices: 166 of 5000 refused at condition number $10^6$ and 4915 of 5000 at $10^8$ in
   `float32`, none from $10^4$ to $10^{14}$ in double
   ([`290-lu-pivot-tolerance.md:58-71`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/docs/derivations/290-lu-pivot-tolerance.md#L58-L71)).
   A smaller step need not cure such a column; use float64.
2. **Fixed factor.** The factor 8 is a choice, not a derived bound.
